_about: Cleanroom policy. Each tool declares which Rule-of-Two property it exercises, the per-tool configuration Meta's post proposes. Roles: read -> [A] untrusted input (a file the agent did not author; a secret file is [B] instead); fetch -> [A]; write -> none (the path is remembered as the agent's own output, so reading it back is not [A]); shell -> [C] when the command leaves the machine, [B] when it names a secret file, [A] when it prints a file the agent did not author. Add a tool here to cover it; a tool that is not listed is observed but exercises no property. secret_files: basename patterns of the files whose values are learned at session start and whose name in a command is [B]. '*.env' is any file with that suffix; a plain name matches only as a whole basename. KEY=VALUE files and JSON files are both read; .env.example never matches.
